data.title: MFB Bancorp, Inc. Announces Commencement of Stock Offering
data.description:
CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mutual Federal Bancorp, Inc. ("Mutual Federal Bancorp") (OTC: "MFDB"), the mid-tier holding company for Mutual Federal Bank (the "Bank"), announced today that MFB Bancorp, Inc. ("MFB Bancorp"), a newly formed Delaware company and the proposed successor holding company of the Bank, has commenced its stock offering in connection with the proposed conversion of Mutual Federal Bancorp, MHC ("Mutual Federal, MHC") from the mutual holding company structure to the stock holding company form of organization.

MFB Bancorp is offering for sale up to 1,035,000 shares (subject to an adjustment to up to 1,190,250 shares) of common stock at a purchase price of $10.00 per share. The shares will be offered in a subscription offering to eligible depositors of the Bank as of March 31, 2025, to the Bank's tax qualified benefit plans and to other eligible members and certain borrowers of the Bank. Shares of common stock that are not subscribed for in the subscription offering may be offered for sale to members of the general public in a community offering with a preference first to natural persons residing in Cook County, Illinois and then to stockholders of Mutual Federal Bancorp as of the close of business on November 9, 2026.

MFB Bancorp's common stock is expected to be quoted on the OTC Markets Group's OTCQB Market under the symbol "MFDB" upon completion of the conversion and stock offering.

All questions concerning the conversion and stock offering or requests for stock offering materials should be directed to the Stock Information Center at (312) 521-1600. The Stock Information Center is open Monday through Friday between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Central Time, except for bank holidays.

Completion of the conversion and stock offering remains subject to final regulatory approvals, the approval of Mutual Federal Bancorp's stockholders and the members of Mutual Federal, MHC, and the sale of at least 765,000 shares of common stock at the minimum of the offering range.

Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC is acting as marketing agent to MFB Bancorp in connection with the stock offering.

This release is neither an offer to sell nor a solicitation of an offer to buy common stock of MFB Bancorp. The offer is made only by MFB Bancorp's prospectus when accompanied by a stock order form. The shares of common stock of MFB Bancorp are not savings accounts or savings deposits, may lose value and are not insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or any other government agency.

MFB Bancorp has filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") a registration statement for the offering to which this press release relates and has filed with the SEC the final prospectus, dated November 10, 2026, for the subscription and community offerings. Before you invest, you should read that prospectus and other documents MFB Bancorp has filed with the SEC for more complete information about MFB Bancorp and the stock offering. You may obtain these documents for free by visiting EDGAR on the SEC website at www.sec.gov.

About Mutual Federal Bancorp

Mutual Federal Bancorp is a federally chartered mid-tier mutual holding company for Mutual Federal Bank, a community-oriented savings association operating from a single location in Chicago, Illinois. The Bank originates one-to-four-family residential real estate loans, multifamily real estate and commercial real estate loans, construction loans and home equity loans and lines of credit. Mutual Federal Bancorp's common stock is quoted on the OTCID Market under the symbol "MFDB".

data.title: Intuit's downbeat outlook deepens Wall Street's anxiety about software companies
data.description:
By Claudia Assis

Software and fintech company to sell Mailchimp business to Bending Spoons

Intuit cut its outlook for fiscal 2027, renewing worries about legacy software companies.

TurboTax maker Intuit is giving investors a fresh reason to worry about legacy software companies.

Intuit's stock (INTU) dropped more than 10% in the after-hours session Thursday after the fintech and software company cut its outlook for fiscal 2027.

That played into concerns that Intuit and other traditional software companies may be ill-equipped to fend off AI disruption and increased competition from AI tools.

Broad worries about software security that surfaced after several recent, well-publicized crashes have played a part. Heading into earnings, Intuit's stock had lost more than 9% on the week, and it was off 53% year to date.

The company also announced a deal to sell its Mailchimp marketing and e-mail business to Italian tech conglomerate Bending Spoons (BSP) for $3.7 billion in cash and stock.

Intuit called for revenue of between $23.1 billion and $23.4 billion for the fiscal year that ends next July. That compares with the FactSet consensus for $23.4 billion. The company in September had modeled revenue of between $23.3 billion and $23.5 billion for the 2027 fiscal year.

The changes centered on Credit Karma, Intuit's consumer credit-monitoring platform, the company said.

Intuit dialed back expectations for Credit Karma's fiscal 2027 revenue to between $2.72 billion and $2.83 billion, from a previous expectation of $2.92 billion to $2.97 billion.

The deal with Bending Spoons for Mailchimp is expected to close early next year, and the outlook will be updated then, Intuit said.

Intuit reported adjusted earnings of $2.91 a share, compared with the FactSet consensus for adjusted earnings of $2.46 a share. Intuit is focused on "disciplined execution as we build durable, long-term growth," CEO Sasan Goodarzi said in a statement.

-Claudia Assis

data.title: Corpay Invests Alongside TPG to Acquire BILL
data.description:
Corpay, Inc. (), the global spend management company, today announced that it has signed a definitive agreement to make a $1.1 billion minority investment in BILL () as part of a transaction to take BILL private alongside TPG for $63.25 per share that values BILL at $6.0 billion.

Under the agreement, Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for an approximately one-third equity stake in the company with the option to acquire 100% of the company. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval and standard closing conditions.

BILL is an intelligent finance platform and leading provider of spend management and accounts payable solutions to small and lower middle market businesses, with an especially unique distribution network of accountants.

“We’re delighted to partner with BILL leadership and TPG on this transaction. Given our successful relationship with TPG, we are excited to participate in this transaction and invest in another large, complementary corporate payments business,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay.

“We expect the transaction to be accretive to Corpay cash EPS in 2027, and the take-private transaction structure gives the company the flexibility to transform and accelerate profit growth. We have the option to buy the rest of the company in 2030,” said Peter Walker, CFO of Corpay.

“Corpay has a long track record of driving value through innovative products and high-quality customer service,” said John Flynn and Tim Millikin, Partners at TPG. “This joint investment is grounded in a shared conviction in the long-term growth opportunities across financial technology and payments where our respective expertise and capabilities will further support BILL’s next chapter of growth.”

Barclays acted as exclusive financial advisor to Corpay, and Sullivan & Cromwell LLP acted as legal counsel to Corpay.

data.title: Gap Q3 Profit Rise 32%; Lowers FY Outlook
data.description:
SAN FRANCISCO (dpa-AFX) - Gap Inc. (GAP), the apparel retailer behind Old Navy, Gap, Banana Republic and Athleta, on Thursday reported higher third-quarter profit, reflecting improved performance at Gap and Old Navy, which offset weakness at Athleta.

The company also lowered its full-year sales and adjusted earnings outlook, citing a slower-than-expected start to the fourth quarter amid warmer weather.

Net income for the quarter increased to $311 million or $0.86 per share from $236 million or $0.62 per share in the prior-year period. Adjusted net income was $296 million, or $0.82 per share, excluding the impact of IEEPA tariff refunds and related interest income.

Net sales rose 2% to $4.01 billion from $3.94 billion a year earlier, while comparable sales were flat against a 5% increase last year. Online sales grew 3% and accounted for 40% of total net sales.

Among its brands, Gap delivered the strongest performance, with net sales rising 11% to $1.06 billion and comparable sales increasing 9%. Old Navy sales advanced 1% to $2.27 billion, while comparable sales were flat. Banana Republic sales declined 3% to $449 million, with comparable sales also down 3%. Athleta recorded a 14% drop in net sales to $220 million, while comparable sales fell 15%.

For fiscal 2026, Gap now expects net sales to be roughly flat, compared with its previous forecast for growth of 1% to 1.5%. Adjusted earnings per share are now expected to range from $2.29 to $2.34, compared with the previous forecast of $2.35 to $2.45. On a reported basis, earnings per share are expected to be approximately $3.71 to $3.76.

For the fourth quarter, the company expects net sales to be flat to down 1% year over year and gross margin of approximately 38.0% to 38.3%.

Separately, Gap announced that Ashley Kechter will become Athleta's next president and CEO.

data.title: Maya stucco heads offer glimpse of ancient artistry in Guatemala
data.description:
By Josue Decavele and Sandra Sebastian

Guatemala has unveiled several expressive, life-sized stucco heads crafted in the Maya period, offering the public a look at what researchers say is a unique concentration of such sculptures from the Maya world.

Dating from the seventh and eighth centuries, the pieces are part of a bigger collection unearthed at the Mirador Basin archaeological site in northern Guatemala in a series of digs over the last decade, impressing researchers with their artistry, state of preservation and the size of the collection.

“There is not a single known example anywhere in the Mayan world of such a large number of sculptures recovered from a single structure,” said Douglas Mauricio, an archaeologist at the Mirador Basin Project.

Major Maya cities grew in prominence beginning 3,000 years ago across a large swathe of present-day southern Mexico and several Central American nations, during a period marked by advances in mathematics, astronomy and art.

The elaborate carvings — showing expressions ranging from scrunched foreheads to broad smiles — highlight the Maya people's mastery of a wide range of artistic skills beyond the mathematics and astronomy for which they are known, said Lilian Vega de Zea, restoration director for the Mirador Basin Project.

“It shows us the advanced technology they had in everything," she said.

The use of colors indicated a complex process involving multiple people — some who prepared the colors, others who mixed the stucco, and a person serving as a model for the head itself, Vega de Zea said.

“These heads represent important people ... they also served as a message to the society of the time, depicting someone who held a certain level of authority.”

The sculptures offer clues about a later period of Maya occupation at El Mirador, when a smaller population returned to the site centuries after its Preclassic peak and maintained the earlier pieces in good condition, Mauricio said.

"They continued to preserve, protect, and hold their Preclassic ancestors in high regard," Mauricio said.

data.title: Activist investor Parvus calls for Accor CEO Bazin to step down, FT reports
data.description:
London-based activist hedge fund Parvus Asset Management has called for Accor's chief executive and chairman, Sebastien Bazin, to step down over what it called poor strategy and capital allocation, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, citing a letter from the investor.

Parvus, which has built a 14% stake in Accor worth €1.6 billion ($1.76 billion), said Bazin, who has led Accor since 2013, had presided over an "unfocused strategy" and "inconsistent capital allocation" and warned it would "hold the board accountable" at the company's next annual general meeting if it did not act, the FT reported.

"In the absence of a satisfactory response or meaningful action, we now consider it necessary to seek changes to the composition of the board and management," Parvus said in the letter seen by the newspaper.

Accor declined to comment, while Parvus did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.

Bazin said at Accor's last annual meeting that the search for his successor was under way and that he would step aside at or before the end of his term in 2028, the report said.

The move comes days after Accor said it intended to acquire the stakes of London-based lifestyle hospitality company Ennismore's minority shareholders in a transaction valued at about €1.6 billion.

Parvus said the deal was a significant decision that should not be made by an outgoing leadership team, the FT reported.

Accor operates more than 5,800 hotels across more than 110 countries. In October, the company raised the lower end of its full-year profit forecast after stronger-than-expected third-quarter growth, driven by its luxury and lifestyle brands and a favorable events calendar.

($1 = 0.9111 euros)

data.title: Gold extends losses below $3,700, pressured by rate-hike bets
data.description:
Gold futures fell for the sixth time in eight sessions to fresh 14-month lows on Thursday, as the market's overwhelming consensus anticipates a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting to combat stubborn inflation.

Minutes from last month's FOMC meeting showed nearly all Fed officials expected interest ​rates will need to move higher, reinforcing sentiments expressed ‌by ⁠several policymakers during the week, including Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who said the central bank may need to respond more aggressively to rising prices.

Traders now see a 94% probability of a 25-bp interest rate boost next month, according to the CME's FedWatch tool, and the dollar index this week reached ​its highest level in 19 months, making dollar-priced gold more expensive for overseas buyers.

Gold prices could fall to $3,500/oz as expectations of interest rate hikes drive bond yields higher and support U.S. dollar strength, FOREX.com analyst Fawad Razaqzada said in a note.

"Rising global bond yields suggest markets are increasingly prepared for the Fed and other central banks to push interest rates higher in their efforts to bring inflation back towards target," Razaqzada wrote, adding that higher real yields are particularly damaging for non-yielding assets such as gold.

"More generally, commodities have seen a wide-ranging selloff, particularly in metals, as volatility in AI valuations raises doubts about longer-term demand for copper or other data center capital inputs," MUFG's Soojin Kim said.

On Thursday, front-month Comex gold for November delivery fell 1.4% to $3,682.10/oz, and front-month Comex November silver slipped 1.5% to $44.318/oz, the lowest settlement for the respective metals since September 19 and 24, 2025.

data.title: BILL Agrees to be Acquired by TPG in Partnership with Corpay
data.description:
BILL (), the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly 500,000 businesses to manage, move, and maximize their money, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay (), the Global Spend Management Company. BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in a cash transaction that values BILL at $6.0 billion. TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm’s U.S. and European private equity platform, and Corpay will acquire a minority interest.

The per share purchase price represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average price ending on November 16, the last full trading day preceding media reports that BILL was in acquisition discussions.

“This transaction marks an exciting new chapter for BILL, delivering significant, certain, and immediate value to our stockholders, while creating new opportunities to accelerate our transformation and deliver greater value to customers,” said René Lacerte, CEO and Founder of BILL. “With our new partners, we will have the resources, expertise, and strategic support to accelerate innovation, advance our AI transformation, and continue to drive the future of financial operations. We look forward to the opportunities ahead for our customers and our business.”

“BILL has built a differentiated financial operations platform that helps small and midsize businesses manage their most critical financial workflows. data.title: Japan Inflation Data Due On Friday
data.description:
HONG KONG (dpa-AFX) - Japan will on Friday release October figures for consumer prices, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

Overall national inflation was flat on month and up 2.1 percent on year in September, while core CPI also rose an annual 2.1 percent.

New Zealand will provide October numbers for credit card spending; in September, spending was up 6.9 percent on year.

Malaysia will see October figures for imports, exports and trade balance. In September, imports were up 52.7 percent on year and exports rose an annual 545 percent for a trade surplus of MYR33.70 billion.

Taiwan will provide October data for export orders and Q3 numbers for current account. In September, export orders surged 62.4 percent on year, while the current account showed a surplus of $58.49 billion in Q2.

Hong Kong will release October figures for consumer prices; in September, overall inflation was up 0.3 percent on month and 1.9 percent on year.

data.title: Keysight Technologies Reports Strong Q4 Net Income Growth
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Keysight Technologies, Inc. (KEYS) on Thursday, reported a sharp increase in net income for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, supported by stronger revenue and a substantial rise in customer orders compared with the prior-year quarter.

Net income climbed to $486 million from $233 million in the three months ended October 31, 2025. Earnings per share increased to $2.82 from $1.35. Revenue advanced 40.5 percent to $1.994 billion from $1.419 billion, while orders surged to $2.339 billion from $1.533 billion.

For the full fiscal year, net income rose to $1.513 billion from $850 million, while revenue increased to $7.157 billion from $5.375 billion. Annual earnings per share reached $8.75, compared with $4.91 a year earlier.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Keysight expects revenue of $2.040 billion to $2.060 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $3.63 to $3.69.

KEYS is currently trading after hours at $284.98, up $3.56 or 1.27 percent on the New York Stock Exchange.

data.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about former CEO, China ties
data.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia related to reports of former CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags," Bonta said, adding that his office was investigating whether China obtained Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information, and if the company misled investors.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

Huang resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia employees.
